bullets.title: Marvell: MS raises PT to $268, announces industry-first 2nm optical interconnect
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley raised its MRVL price target to $268 from $246. Separately, Marvell announced what it calls the "industry-first 2nm optical interconnect" demonstration, positioned as a next-generation AI data center connectivity advance.

bullets.title: Wells Fargo raises META PT to $796 from $640, maintains Overweight
bullets.body: Wells Fargo significantly raised its Meta Platforms price target to $796 from $640, maintaining an Overweight rating. The $156 PT increase represents a substantial 24% lift to the prior target.

bullets.title: TSMC: Four 1.4nm plants targeted for Q2 2028 at only marginal premium to N2 pricing
bullets.body: TSMC reportedly plans to bring four 1.4nm node fabs online by Q2 2028, with wafer pricing only marginally above N2 levels. The modest price step-up could be a positive demand signal if yields ramp as planned.

bullets.title: DeepSeek bets on Huawei chips; expects Q4 delivery — negative read for US semis
bullets.body: DeepSeek is prioritizing domestic chips and expects Huawei chip deliveries as early as Q4, per reports. The shift underscores a sustained workaround to US export controls on advanced AI semiconductors to China.

bullets.title: Intel substrate capacity concern flagged; Qualcomm CPU (codenamed Rolex) requires EMIB-T packaging
bullets.body: A chip industry observer raised concern that Intel may not have secured sufficient substrate capacity to support all customer demand. Separately, Qualcomm's large CPU — codenamed Rolex — reportedly requires EMIB-T advanced chiplet interconnect, raising questions about fab dependency.

bullets.title: NVIDIA RTX 60 'Rubin' GPUs reportedly slated for 2028 launch
bullets.body: NVIDIA is reportedly planning to launch its RTX 60 consumer GPU lineup, codenamed Rubin, in 2028. The timeline is far out but is described as strategically sensible.

bullets.title: ams OSRAM 25μm microLED VCSEL platform targets AI scale-up networks; press release reportedly edited
bullets.body: ams OSRAM unveiled a thin-film microVCSEL platform with 25μm dense pitch for AI interconnect applications, matching Avicena's next-gen specs. One observer flagged that ams OSRAM's press release was quietly edited after publication, removing a specific detail about a 1,024-emitter array that would imply ~4 Tbps aggregate throughput (32 Gbps × 1,024 ÷ 8).

bullets.title: Xi Jinping to visit US Sept 23-25 — China also plans to drop 15% LNG tariff this week
bullets.body: China confirmed Xi Jinping's first US visit in nearly three years, scheduled September 23-25. Separately, China plans to drop a 15% tariff on US LNG this week, potentially reopening energy trade and setting the stage for new deals. Markets are anticipating a constructive outcome from Trump-Xi meetings.

bullets.title: Google fined €403M by Irish DPA over location data handling
bullets.body: Ireland's Data Protection Authority fined Google €403 million for violations related to location data handling practices.

bullets.title: Amazon blocks AI assistant from shopping on its platform
bullets.body: Amazon has reportedly blocked an AI assistant from making purchases on its e-commerce platform, raising questions about how the company will manage agentic AI commerce competition.

bullets.title: 'Streamflation' driving mass subscription cancellations: 39% of Americans cancelled in past 6 months
bullets.body: 39% of Americans cancelled at least one streaming subscription in the past six months, up sharply from 29% in March, with repeated price hikes and broader cost-of-living pressure cited as key drivers.

bullets.title: Fed's Goolsbee: inflation path 'won't be painless'; rate cuts need convincing evidence
bullets.body: Chicago Fed's Goolsbee flagged persistent supply shocks — energy, tariffs — as complicating inflation's return to 2%, stating the credible path back is "hard to see." He affirmed "no ambiguity" that the Fed would tighten if demand overheats, and stressed Fed independence amid external pressure for cheaper borrowing costs.

bullets.title: Oil falls 4th day; JPMorgan oil team abandons Iran war scenario forecasting
bullets.body: Brent crude fell ~2% to ~$101.77/bbl as Iran diplomacy hopes and partial Saudi supply recovery weighed on prices. JPMorgan's oil team reportedly gave up forecasting Iran war endgame scenarios, citing Trump policy unpredictability moving past prior economic redlines.

bullets.title: Diesel hits record $6.51/gal; refined products diverging from crude decline
bullets.body: US diesel prices surged to a record $6.51/gallon and regular gasoline approached $4.50/gallon, driven by Middle East energy flow disruptions and Russian refinery constraints. Notably, refined product prices are moving in the opposite direction from falling international crude prices.

bullets.title: Hormuz crisis: supertanker rates hit $1M+/day, ~5x pre-war levels; traffic collapses
bullets.body: Supertanker rates on the Persian Gulf-to-China route hit $1.035M/day, approximately 5x pre-war levels, as traffic through the Strait of Hormuz collapsed to just 17 commodity vessel crossings over the weekend.

bullets.title: Bitcoin rallies to $85K+, highest since January; macro risk-on read
bullets.body: Bitcoin climbed above $85,117 — its highest level since January 29 — gaining ~4% on the session. The move coincides with global stock rally, lower oil, and pre-Xi summit optimism.

bullets.title: Macro regime: profitable Russell 2000 stocks outperforming by ~500bps; healthcare long vs. IWM short generating alpha
bullets.body: In 2024, profitable Russell 2000 stocks are outperforming unprofitable ones by ~500bps, reversing last year's 1,000bps advantage for loss-makers. Separately, one macro framework reports long healthcare (XLV +12.7% over 3 months) vs. short IWM (-4.0%) as a high-conviction 'Quad 2' expression.

bullets.title: Yen weakening sharply; copper surges 1.7% to bullish trend; yield curve flattening
bullets.body: USD/JPY continues to strengthen after the yen fell 2.5% last week and is declining again Monday. Copper popped another 1.7% after returning to a bullish trend signal. The yield curve is flattening, with peak US growth cycle now in the rearview mirror per one macro framework.

bullets.title: Palantir executive Chad Wahl interviewed live on X
bullets.body: A fintwit account hosted a live interview with Palantir's Chad Wahl at 10AM ET on X, a potential venue for company commentary outside standard IR channels.
